title: 計算論
subtitle: Theory of Computation
educationalGoal: Computers can be used to solve various kinds of problems. Here a question arises; “Can computers solve any problem?” The theory of computability can provide an answer to that question. Some problems take extremely long time to be solved and they are called `intractable problems'. The theory of complexity deals with intractable problems.
advice: In this course, we introduce the Turing machine, a formal model of computation. Students will learn computable and incomputable problems by means of the Turing machine. Some classes on computable problems will be provided and students will learn the relationship between these classes. The primary topics are as follows: 1. Turing machine as algorithm 2. Incomputable problems 3. Complexity class 4. Intractable problems On the whole, the topics are abstract. Therefore, solving problems independently is important for gaining a sufficient level of understanding.
books: オートマトン 言語理論 計算論II[第2版],J.ホップクロフト,R.モトワニ,J.ウルマン著,サイエンス社
requiredKnowledge: It is desirable for students to have taken "Formal language and automata". Prior knowledge of formal language is especially helpful although it is also taught in the course.

activityGoals.body: Be able to explain the movements of a Turing machine.
Be able to explain the definition of recursively enumerable language.
Be able to explain at least one example belonging to class P.
Be able to explain the difference between class P and class NP.
Be able to explain NP completeness.
